title: Installing SQL tools: Windows, macOS, and Linux

QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.

spans.code:
SELECT sqlite_version();
-- Windows: install official SQLite CLI and add it to PATH
-- macOS: brew install sqlite
-- Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install sqlite3
-- Verify: sqlite3 --version

spans.text: The engine version is displayed; the exact value depends on the installed version.

A SQL setup has two parts: a database engine and a tool for writing queries and viewing results. SQLite is a friendly start because it runs in one file without a server; DB Browser for SQLite adds a graphical interface. On Windows, download the command-line tools from SQLite's official download page and add their folder to PATH. On macOS, Homebrew can install them with `brew install sqlite`; on Debian/Ubuntu use `sudo apt install sqlite3`. For other Linux distributions, use their official package manager. PostgreSQL provides official installers and OS-specific instructions for all three systems. DB Browser packages are also available for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Verify with `sqlite3 --version`, open a practice file with `sqlite3 school.db`, and exit with `.quit`.

Key line: `SELECT sqlite_version();`
What it does: Check SQLite with sqlite3 --version; sqlite3 school.db opens a local database file.
Why it is used: Use the official download source and choose a package matching your OS and processor architecture.
If omitted or changed: SQLite CLI and DB Browser can use the same SQLite engine; one is a terminal interface and the other is graphical.
